note: Culture areas for the Eras level. Each area groups country columns that a published periodization covers; its eras are the rows of that periodization, read from the cited Wikipedia revision (wikipedia-eras.json). Columns outside every area, and the years after an area's last era, use the region's period bins with their leading states computed from the data. Which columns an area covers is an editorial choice, explained in each note.

areas.label: Eastern North America
areas.note: Periods of the Eastern Woodlands from the table of North American archaeological periods. Southern Canada is included because the table lists Canadian Hopewellian complexes (Point Peninsula, Laurel, Saugeen) in the Middle Woodland. The Arctic, the Plains and the Southwest have their own sequences; their cultures appear at the deeper levels.

areas.label: Mesoamerica
areas.note: The summary table of Mesoamerican chronology. Mesoamerica covers central and southern Mexico, Guatemala, Belize, El Salvador and western Honduras; northern Mexico lies outside it but shares the column. The Terminal Classic (800–900/1000) overlaps the Late Classic and is folded into it here.

areas.label: Antilles
areas.note: The three ages of Caribbean prehistory as given in the list of pre-Columbian cultures (citing Rouse 1992). They describe the Greater and Lesser Antilles as a whole; not every island was settled in every age.

areas.label: Bahamas
areas.note: The list names the Bahamas only for the Lucayans of the Late Ceramic Age (700–1500 AD).

areas.label: Andes
areas.note: Rowe and Lanning's periods for 'Peru and the Andean Region'. The list of pre-Columbian cultures uses the same periods for cultures in Colombia, Ecuador, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina, so those columns share them; the periods describe their Andean parts. The list dates the Early Horizon to 900 BC–200 AD and the Early Intermediate to 200–600 AD; the periodization article, used here, has 900–200 BCE and 200 BCE–600 CE.
